Guides

Plugins without the SDK

This guide is for an author who writes a plugin in a language that has no Ilium SDK, such as Go, C or Python, or who wants to build a component straight from the WIT files. It states what the host requires of the component, what the Rust and TypeScript SDKs write for you and you must now write yourself, what ilium plugin build does with an unknown language, and how to check the result. Two SDKs exist: Rust SDK and TypeScript SDK.

Requirement ids such as DEV-302 are in Requirements: developer tooling. Ids such as PKG-139 are in Requirements: manifest and package.

You will need

  • The contract listing WIT reference (ilium:plugin@0.1.0). It is the only source of the types and function names.
  • A toolchain that turns WIT into a WebAssembly component: wit-bindgen for Go (TinyGo) or C, or componentize-py for Python.
  • The Ilium CLI, for ilium plugin test --conformance (Conformance suite).

Support status

Part Status
The contract (WIT files, error record, limits, ilium:api-version section) Supported. A component that meets it runs like an SDK plugin.
The Rust and TypeScript SDKs and their toolchains in ilium plugin build Supported.
A language toolchain for Go, C, Python or any other language Community-supported. The project does not test it, does not fix its bugs, and does not promise that a version of it keeps producing valid components.

The host cannot tell what language made a component. It sees a WebAssembly component, its exports and its custom section. It applies the same checks, limits, deadlines and traps to every component (Runtime model).

What the host requires of the component

The install check is the same for every component. It is defined in Package format. The rows that matter for a hand-built component:

Id Rule Failure code
[PKG-141] The file MUST be a component (layer 1 in the preamble), not a core module. wit-bindgen and componentize-py produce a core module first; wrap it as a component before you ship. package.component-invalid
[PKG-142] The component MUST validate against the world named in the manifest. Exports that the manifest does not list, or the reverse, are refused. package.component-invalid, manifest.exports-mismatch
[PKG-138] The component MUST contain exactly one custom section named ilium:api-version. package.api-section-missing, package.api-section-repeated
[PKG-139] The payload MUST be 6 bytes: major, minor and patch as three big-endian u16. For ilium:plugin@0.1.0 it is 00 00 00 01 00 00. package.api-section-invalid
[PKG-140] The three integers MUST equal the version in the manifest api key. manifest.api-version

The manifest api value is the string ilium:plugin@0.1.0 (Manifest reference). It is also the value the host puts in activation.api, and the host compares versions before linking (ABI-021).

The section the SDK writes

The SDK build writes the section at stage 5 of the build (DEV-302). Without the SDK you write it yourself, after the component exists, with any tool that adds a custom section to a component, such as wasm-tools. Add it once. Running the step twice on the same file makes two sections and the install fails with package.api-section-repeated. Check the result by reading the file back: the section name is exactly ilium:api-version, the payload is six bytes.

Export names

A plugin component targets one of the worlds in WIT reference. The world base exports two interfaces and the others add one each:

World Exports
base ilium:exports/lifecycle@0.1.0 (activate, deactivate) and ilium:exports/handler@0.1.0 (on-events)
with-detector adds ilium:exports/detector@0.1.0 (identify, classify)
with-jobs adds ilium:exports/job-runner@0.1.0 (run)
with-service adds ilium:exports/service-provider@0.1.0

The component must export exactly the interfaces its manifest lists (PKG-142). A generator names the functions after the WIT names, in the style of its language: on-events becomes OnEvents in Go and on_events in C and Python. The names in the component binary are always the WIT names.

What the SDK does that you must now do

Duty What the SDK does What you do
API section Writes ilium:api-version at build Write it once, see above
Error record Turns Result<T, PluginError> or a thrown PluginError into result<T, plugin-error> Return the WIT record: code (one of the 15 error-code values, in the order of the enum), message (at most 256 characters, plain text) and retry-after-ms. See Errors and limits. A code outside the enum cannot be encoded, so the generator rejects it.
Restore bytes Returns the bytes you give it from deactivate Return option<list<u8>>. The host stores the bytes without reading them, drops anything over 1 MiB, and hands them back as activation.restored (Persistence and restart, LIF-152). The layout is yours. Start it with a format byte and fall back to defaults when the first byte is unknown (AUT-206).
Limits Rejects some bad calls before they leave the plugin Keep to the caps yourself: at most 256 events in and 256 submissions out per on-events call, deadlines of 20 ms for on-events, 10 ms for render, 2000 ms for activate and 500 ms for deactivate (Performance). A breach traps the instance exactly as it does for an SDK plugin.
Async calls Wraps a request-id and its take-* partner in a future Call the request-id function, wait for the completion event in on-events, then call the take-* function. The rules are in the WIT comments of each function.
Pure render Gives you the view target and area render may not call a host function that submits intents. Return a ui-tree.

Debug aid: a plugin that traps shows at <function> in the trap message only when the component keeps the names of its exports. Keep them in release builds (DEV-303).

What ilium plugin build does with another language

ilium plugin build detects the language from the project files (DEV-002). A Cargo.toml means Rust and a package.json means TypeScript. A project with neither fails with toolchain.language-unknown, exit 4, and nothing is written. A project with both fails with toolchain.language-ambiguous. There is no flag that selects a third toolchain, and build never runs wit-bindgen, componentize-py or any other tool you name.

Build the component with your own toolchain, outside ilium plugin build. Two points follow from the CLI reference:

  • ilium plugin pack reads dist/build.json and refuses a missing or stale dist/ with pack.not-built or pack.stale-build (DEV-095). The build.json record is written only by build.
  • The CLI reference defines no build --component flag and no pack --prebuilt flag. Packing an externally built component is therefore not a supported CLI path in this contract version. Until the CLI documents one, treat a non-SDK plugin as testable but not packable with the project tools.

What you can do today is run the component through the same harness the SDK plugins use. ilium plugin test --component <file> loads the file you name instead of dist/<side>.wasm and runs the fixtures in component mode (Plugin command-line reference, DEV-080). The component is checked with the real linker, limits and deadlines.

The acceptance check

ilium plugin test --conformance is the acceptance check for a plugin in any language. It does not look at the language, the toolchain or the SDK. It needs the component at dist/<side>.wasm (subject plugin), so copy the externally built file there first. It loads the component, drives it with the fixed cases of Conformance suite and prints one conformance record per case and a summary. Any fail makes the exit code 3 (DEV-602). A pass means the component keeps to the contract limits. A case that needs a grant the manifest does not request is skipped with the reason grant-not-requested (DEV-600).

The subjects sdk and host are refused in a normal install with usage.subject-unavailable (DEV-601). They are for the Ilium source tree. A host author who wants to claim conformance uses the published corpus instead: each case has an input, an expected result and a matrix row, and a host may claim a version only when every case of that version passes (ABI-073 to ABI-075, Host conformance).

The suite does not check the look of a view, the speed on a given machine, or the quality of the language toolchain (The edge of the suite). For parity of outcomes between the Rust and TypeScript SDKs there are separate cases (DEV-927). A third language has no such parity promise.

Failure modes

Symptom Cause Fix
toolchain.language-unknown The project folder has neither Cargo.toml nor package.json Build with your own toolchain, or keep a Cargo.toml or package.json only if you really use that SDK
package.component-invalid A core module, or a component that does not fit the world Wrap the module as a component against the world in the manifest
manifest.exports-mismatch The component exports more or fewer interfaces than the manifest lists Make the manifest and the component list the same interfaces
package.api-section-missing The section was not added Add ilium:api-version once
package.api-section-repeated The step ran twice Remove one section
package.api-section-invalid The payload is not 6 bytes Write three big-endian u16
manifest.api-version The three numbers differ from the manifest api Make them equal to ilium:plugin@0.1.0
A trap with restore warnings Restore bytes over 1 MiB, or a layout the next version cannot read Keep the bytes small and start them with a format byte
